Confusable pairs among the equipment standards, scanning habits, signal distances and hand signals, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
Brake and turn lights must show for at least 100 feet in daylight, and they may either share the taillight housing or be mounted on their own. [A01]
Why it matters: group lights; difficulty medium; confusable combined versus separate lamps.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
With anti-lock brakes you press hard and hold steady, which is the opposite of pumping the pedal. [A01]
Why it matters: group braking; difficulty medium; misconception target.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
Under-inflated tires wear fast and risk blowouts, while over-inflated tires lose grip and wear the middle of the tread. [A01]
Why it matters: group tires; difficulty medium; confusable under versus over inflation.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A01
A tire becomes unsafe below 1/16 inch of tread, while the brake pedal must stay at least one-third of its travel above the floor. [A01]
Why it matters: group equipment limits; difficulty high; confusable fraction values.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A02
The horn must be heard from at least 200 feet, yet it must not give an unreasonably loud or harsh sound, so both limits apply at once. [A02]
Why it matters: group horn; difficulty medium; confusable minimum audibility versus maximum harshness.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A02
Hazard flashers may be used by any vehicle, while emergency lights and sirens are reserved for law enforcement and emergency vehicles. [A02]
Why it matters: group warning devices; difficulty medium; confusable flashers versus emergency lights.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A03
Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead of the car, but check the mirrors about every 10 seconds. [A03]
Why it matters: group scanning; difficulty high; confusable look-ahead time versus mirror interval.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A03
Mirrors show the scene behind, but the rear-corner blind spots need a quick look over the shoulder. [A03]
Why it matters: group scanning; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0070]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A04
Signal at least 100 feet before a turn or stop in general, and at least 200 feet before a turn where the limit is 45 mph or more. [A04]
Why it matters: group signaling; difficulty high; confusable normal versus higher-speed distance.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A04
Arm straight out means a left turn, forearm up means a right turn, and arm pointed down means slowing or stopping. [A04]
Why it matters: group hand signals; difficulty medium; confusable right turn versus stop.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A04
With unequal dangers give more room to the most likely one, but with equal dangers stop and let oncoming traffic go by. [A04]
Why it matters: group adjusting; difficulty medium; confusable unequal versus equal hazards.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0071]
